chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: Arranging for Fletcher Henderson, in his own style
summary: Henderson, busy writing for Benny Goodman, hired Randolph to arrange for his band, the Grand Terrace band with Roy Eldridge and Chu Berry.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Same way with Fletcher Henderson. I arranged with Fletcher.
Arranging for him. See, Fletcher was arranging for Benny, and he was getting me to arrange for him.
Right, because he had a band at that time also.
Because he had a band, and he told me, he said, he never did get my name right. Zilner, he always said Zalner --

And he says, Zalner, I still feel the name Fletcher Henderson means something to the people, so but I'm hooked up here, writing for Benny. And I still want my band to go on. But, you see, when -- I guess you know, when you write for those bands, you can't take the arrangements and you can't take the scores yourself and --
But did you write in his style?
You wrote in your own style?
Was that the Grand Terrace Graham Harris band? In the '36 band?
Yeah, that was the Grand Terrace Graham Harris band.
Oh, that was a good band.
Did they ever record any of your arrangements?
I don't know. I don't know whether they did or not. Because I was moving and getting around so fast. I was a much younger man than I am now, so --
